question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager complained that Sheetal's email was not __up to the standard__ for the company.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "up to the mark".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"up to the mark"** means to meet the required standard or quality; satisfactory or acceptable. (मानक के अनुरूप)

 
 
• **Example:** The teacher felt that the student's essay was not up to the mark and needed improvement.
 
 
 
• The given phrase **"up to the standard"** also means meeting the required level or quality but is less commonly used in comparison to "up to the mark." (मानक के अनुरूप)
 
 
• **Example:** The hotel facilities were up to the standard expected by international travelers.
 
 
 
• Both phrases imply the same meaning, but "up to the mark" is more appropriate and widely used in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: an uphill task** (दुर्लभ कार्य): Refers to a task that is very challenging or difficult to accomplish.

 
 
• **Example:** Completing the project in such a short time will be an uphill task.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: up and doing** (सक्रिय): Refers to being active and energetic in getting things done.
 
 
• **Example:** After her recovery, she was up and doing, ready to tackle new challenges.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: under the nose** (आंखों के सामने): Refers to something happening right in front of someone without them noticing.
 
 
• **Example:** The thief stole the wallet under the nose of the security guard.
